newsitem.title: UK: Entergy has met UK authorities on London bid.
newsitem.headline: Entergy has met UK authorities on London bid.

text.p: U.S. group Entergy Corp has already met UK authorities to discuss its agreed 1.267 billion stg bid for regional electricity company London Electricity, executives told a press conference.
"We met with the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) on Tuesday and had a conversation with the regulator (Offer)," Entergy chairman Ed Lupberger said.
He said Entergy was "able to assure (Offer) that we would comply with all the assurances he put forward."
The bid, which values London at 705 pence per share, was announced by the two companies earlier on Wednesday.

It still awaits UK approval but observers felt this was likely after the DTI approved an agreed $2.15 billion bid for East Midlands from Dominion Resources of the U.S. on Wednesday and CalEnergy's hostile bid for Northern Electric on Friday.
The DTI "will understand the value that Entergy brings," Lupberger added.
Lupberger said no decisions had yet been made on any management changes and cases would be looked at on an individual basis.
He said Entergy had looked at other Recs on a preliminary basis but London was "our best alternative."

Entergy executives said there had been no direct contact with any Northern Electric executives, contrary to newspaper reports cited by CE Electric, CalEnergy's bid vehicle, in a statement on Wednesday.
